sonnet.problem: The card cites Isaiah 46:1, 3, but its text only tells verse 1 (Bel and Nebo crouching). Verse 3 is not used on this card, so the citation is wider than what the card tells.
sonnet.rule: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

sonnet.problem: This true/false card asks about verse 4 before any earlier card has told it. Card 9 tells verse 4 only afterward. The statement itself carries the whole claim, so a baker has nothing to reason from and can only guess or repeat what the question says.
sonnet.rule: A choice card can look back at a verse an earlier card in the same stop told, but never jumps ahead.

sonnet.problem: The joke "No memo, friend, He paints a PICTURE" makes the way God speaks, and the way Scripture is written (a picture rather than a plain statement), the punchline.
sonnet.rule: Holy things, like the ark, and the way Scripture is written are never the joke.

sonnet.problem: The right answer "It will not be delayed" is a negation, while the wrong answers are time phrases. The two wrong answers, "After many generations" and "Only at the end of time", both mean "much later", so they mean nearly the same as each other. The right answer stands out in kind and form.
sonnet.rule: Two wrong answers never mean the same as each other either.
